nodes.summary: For an index type $n$, a belief about the state consists of a mean $m \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and a covariance matrix $P$, an arbitrary real $n \times n$ matrix. It describes the Gaussian distribution $N(m, P)$ when $P$ is positive semidefinite (the belief is valid); for other matrices Mathlib's multivariate Gaussian is a junk value. Prediction with positive semidefinite process noise, update with positive definite…
nodes.title: Gaussian belief

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $w$ be measurable random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v$ a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^p$ on a probability space, with $x$ independent of $w$ and the pair $(x, w)$ independent of $v$. Suppose $x$ has the law $N(m, P)$ of a belief with mean $m$ and positive semidefinite covariance $P$, $w$ has law $N(0, Q)$ and $v$ has law $N(0, R)$, with $Q$ and $R$ positive semidefinite. nodes.title: One filter step is the exact posterior

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v$ a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^p$ on a probability space, with $x$ independent of $v$. Suppose $x$ has the law $N(m, P)$ of a belief with mean $m$ and positive semidefinite covariance $P$, and $v$ has law $N(0, R)$ with $R$ positive semidefinite. Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix with $H P H^\top + R$ invertible, and put $Y = H x + v$.…
nodes.title: The update step is the exact posterior

nodes.summary: For a real $p \times n$ matrix $H$, a real $p \times p$ matrix $R$ and a belief with covariance $P$, the Kalman gain is the real $n \times p$ matrix $K = P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1}$, where the inverse is taken to be $0$ when $H P H^\top + R$ is singular.
nodes.title: Kalman gain

nodes.summary: The law of a belief with mean $m$ and covariance $P$ is Mathlib's multivariate Gaussian measure $N(m, P)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. It is the Gaussian distribution with mean $m$ and covariance $P$ when $P$ is positive semidefinite (the belief is valid); otherwise it is the point mass at $m$.
nodes.title: Law of a belief

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $w$ be measurable, independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ on a probability space. If $x$ has the law $N(m, P)$ of a belief with mean $m$ and positive semidefinite covariance $P$, and $w$ has law $N(0, Q)$ with $Q$ positive semidefinite, then for every real $n \times n$ matrix $F$ the random vector $F x + w$ has the law of the predicted belief, $N(F m, F P F^\top + Q)$.
nodes.title: The predict step is exact

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $Q$ be real $n \times n$ matrices with $Q$ positive semidefinite. If a belief is valid, that is, its covariance $P$ is positive semidefinite, then the predicted belief, with covariance $F P F^\top + Q$, is valid.
nodes.title: Prediction preserves validity

nodes.summary: Given real $n \times n$ matrices $F$ and $Q$, the prediction of a belief with mean $m$ and covariance $P$ is the belief with mean $F m$ and covariance $F P F^\top + Q$. It models the dynamics $x' = F x + w$ with process noise $w \sim N(0, Q)$.
nodes.title: Kalman prediction

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $Q$ be real $n \times n$ matrices with $Q$ positive semidefinite, $H$ a real $p \times n$ matrix, $R$ a positive definite real $p \times p$ matrix and $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$. If a belief is valid (its covariance is positive semidefinite), then so is the belief obtained from it by one filter step with $F$, $Q$, $H$, $R$ and the observation $y$.
nodes.title: A filter step preserves validity

nodes.summary: Given real $n \times n$ matrices $F$ and $Q$, a real $p \times n$ matrix $H$, a real $p \times p$ matrix $R$ and an observation $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$, one filter step sends a belief to the update, with $H$, $R$ and $y$, of its prediction with $F$ and $Q$.
nodes.title: Kalman filter step

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix, $R$ a real $p \times p$ matrix and $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$, and let a belief have covariance $P$. Then the covariance of the belief updated with $H$, $R$ and $y$ equals $P - P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1} H P$. Here $M^{-1}$ is the matrix inverse, taken to be $0$ when $M$ is singular, so no invertibility is assumed.
nodes.title: Schur form of the updated covariance

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix, $R$ a symmetric positive definite real $p \times p$ matrix and $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$. If a belief is valid, then the belief updated with $H$, $R$ and $y$ is valid.
nodes.title: The Kalman update preserves validity

nodes.summary: Given a real $p \times n$ observation matrix $H$, a real $p \times p$ matrix $R$, an observation $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a belief with mean $m$ and covariance $P$, the updated belief has mean $m + K (y - H m)$ and covariance $(I - K H) P$, where $K = P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1}$ is the Kalman gain and the matrix inverse is taken to be $0$ when $H P H^\top + R$ is singular.
nodes.title: Kalman filter update

nodes.summary: A belief is valid when its covariance matrix is positive semidefinite.
nodes.title: Valid Gaussian beliefs

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
